disclaimer: Reminder reference only - NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set by territorial regulation and can change. Always verify current regulations with the Government of the Northwest Territories, Environment and Climate Change. Trapping in the NWT is governed by the Wildlife Act, S.N.W.T. 2013, c. 30 and the Trapping Regulations continued under it. Aboriginal and treaty harvest rights and land-claim settlement-area rules layer over territorial law and are only partly modelled here. This dataset is for the separate Canada clone of Opossum Foot; it is NOT part of the US app, which stays US-only and untouched.

license_summary.certified_traps: Only AIHTS-certified traps may be used in the NWT: the GNWT Summary states it is unlawful for any person to use traps not listed in the regulations, and that only certified traps listed under the Agreement on International Humane Trapping Standards may be used. See the 'aihts' section of this dataset.
license_summary.export: A wildlife export permit is required to export wildlife from the NWT (no fee under the Fees Regulations); non-residents require one for big game. A federal CITES export permit is required to export CITES-listed species (including wolf, lynx and otter) from Canada.
license_summary.fees_not_verified: The General Hunting Licence fee itself was NOT verified from the Fees Regulations schedule in this pass. Do not quote a GHL price until the schedule is read directly. See verification.known_gaps.
license_summary.fees_verified: From the Wildlife Fees Regulations, R-114-2014 (consolidation): registered trapping area licence $24; membership in a registered group trapping area — no fee; authorization to trap furbearers under a Special Harvester Licence $24; small game authorization on a hunting licence $24 (resident/SHL), $48 (non-resident), $119 (non-resident alien); wildlife export permit — no fee; fur dealer licence $475, renewal $238.
license_summary.gmvf_program: The Genuine Mackenzie Valley Fur (GMVF) program markets NWT wild fur, complies with the AIHTS, and takes fur in through Renewable Resource Officers. The GNWT also publishes an annual NWT Trapper's calendar and a GMVF Trapper Education Manual.
license_summary.harvest_reporting: No Ontario-style mandatory season-end harvest report was found in published GNWT material in this pass. ECC runs carcass and sample collections and GMVF fur is submitted through Renewable Resource Officers; whether a formal trapper harvest-reporting duty exists in the Trapping Regulations is unverified — see known_gaps.
license_summary.hunter_education: As of January 1, 2020, all resident and non-resident hunters must complete Hunter Education training before being issued a hunting licence in the NWT, unless exempt under the regulations (GNWT Summary).
license_summary.land_claims: Land-claim settlement regions layer over territorial law: the Inuvialuit Settlement Region, Gwich'in Settlement Area, Sahtu Settlement Area, Tłı̨chǫ lands, and the Dehcho (no final agreement). A licensed trapper may not harvest the following without permission from the land-claim organization: ground squirrel, red squirrel, marmot and hare in the Inuvialuit Settlement Region; ground squirrel, red squirrel and marmot in the Gwich'in Settlement Area; red squirrel and marmot in the Sahtu Settlement Area; woodchuck and red squirrel on Tłı̨chǫ lands (ECC). Co-management boards (WMAC, Gwich'in Renewable Resources Board, Sahtu Renewable Resources Board, Wek'èezhı̀ı Renewable Resources Board) and local Hunters and Trappers Committees / Renewable Resources Councils recommend or set conditions that the territorial regulation alone does not show.
license_summary.licence_types: General Hunting Licence (GHL) — an Aboriginal person who is a member or eligible to be a member of an NWT organization listed in the regulations; Resident Hunting Licence (Canadian citizen or landed immigrant resident in the NWT for 12 continuous months); Non-resident and Non-resident Alien Hunting Licences; Special Harvester Licence (SHL). Wildlife Act s. 45(1): no person shall trap furbearers unless authorized by a general hunting licence, a special harvester licence or a permit — subject to the s. 17 rights exception.
license_summary.registered_trapping_areas: Registered trapping areas and registered group trapping areas carry exclusive trapping rights for the holder or members. Several Summary season rows are specific to the Fort Good Hope Registered Group Trapping Area (FGH RGTA) and are modelled as their own season rows.
license_summary.rights_based_harvest: A person exercising an Aboriginal or treaty right needs NO licence to trap in their traditional area, and there are NO set trapping seasons for rights-based harvest in the harvester's traditional use area (ECC). The 'AH' season rows in this dataset reproduce the GNWT Summary's Jul 1 - Jun 30 spans for Aboriginal harvesters: they record the ABSENCE of a closed season, not a territorial open season, and must be modelled and labelled that way in the clone. One exception: lynx — the Summary gives Aboriginal harvesters a set season (Nov 15 - Apr 15) in area I/LX/01 only.
license_summary.season_housekeeping: Trapping equipment must not be set before the first day of a season and must be removed or rendered harmless by the last day of the season (GNWT Summary, fur-trapper rules).
license_summary.special_harvester_licence: An SHL can be issued to a person who does not have Aboriginal harvesting rights in an area but is supporting an Indigenous family, living a subsistence lifestyle, or given permission to trap or harvest more than a Resident, Non-resident or General Hunting Licence allows. An SHL cannot be used outside the seasons, limits or conditions applicable to Aboriginal harvesters under the Big Game Hunting, Small Game Hunting and Trapping Regulations. All SHLs expire June 30 following the date of issue.
license_summary.trap_check: Live-hold restraining traps (soft-catch traps and leg snares that hold an animal alive) must be checked at least once every 72 hours (ECC). No check interval for killing traps was published in the sources read in this pass.
license_summary.wastage: It is an offence to waste the pelt of bear*, beaver*, coyote, ermine (stoat), fisher, fox, least weasel, lynx, marten, mink, muskrat*, otter, skunk, wolf or wolverine. *Bear, beaver and muskrat pelts may be discarded where the animal was harvested for meat.

verification.confirmation_notes: All trapping season dates were transcribed from the GNWT Summary of Hunting and Trapping Regulations' 'Fur Trappers Only' tables (2021-22 edition — verified byte-identical by MD5 to the file ECC currently serves, i.e. still the newest edition posted online) and mapped into the 2026-27 regulatory year (Jul 1, 2026 - Jun 30, 2027): fall dates fall in 2026, winter/spring dates in 2027. Calendar checks: 2027 is not a leap year, so Feb 28, 2027 is the last day of February 2027; every close date falls on or before Jun 30, 2027. The Trapping Regulations themselves carried over unchanged at the Wildlife Act (2013) transition per GNWT's July 2014 Phase-1 document; last amendment located is R-008-2017. Fees verified against the Wildlife Fees Regulations R-114-2014 consolidation. Species-at-risk statuses verified against GNWT's Species at Risk in the NWT (2024) and nwtspeciesatrisk.ca. Report-a-poacher line 1-866-POACHER (762-2437) verified in the Summary (p. 60). Zone letters D, G, I, R, S, U and area codes (I/LX/01, I/WF/01-05, R/TC/01, FGH RGTA) are as published in the Summary.

Season dates therefore rest on the GNWT Summary — the regulator's own publication of the Trapping Regulations seasons — cross-checked against the Wildlife Act (2013) and GNWT's 2014 Phase-1 transition document. Last Trapping Regulations amendment located: R-008-2017; a search of 2022-2025 Gazette indexes for later amendments was inconclusive. RESOLVE BY: pulling the consolidated Trapping Regulations from the NWT Legislation Division or CanLII when accessible and diffing every date.

No post-2021-22 edition of the Summary of Hunting and Trapping Regulations is posted on the ECC website (the 2021-22 PDF is byte-identical to the live file, MD5-verified). RESOLVE BY: asking ECC or checking a regional office for a current print edition.

Red squirrel, marmot, hare, woodchuck, ground squirrel: land-claim exclusivity rules are documented (ECC), and small game HUNTING seasons are published, but whether a GHL trapping season exists for any of them (e.g. red squirrel for the fur trade) is not stated in published sources read. aihts.models_note: The NWT publishes NO territorial schedules of certified traps equivalent to Ontario's O. Reg. 667/98 Schedules 1 and 2, so no per-species model counts are recorded here — entering Ontario's counts would misstate the NWT position. The operative list is the Fur Institute of Canada's national certified-trap list, which the NWT points trappers to. Model-by-model transcription of the FIC list for the NWT species set is a defined follow-on task.
aihts.note: The NWT implements the AIHTS by requiring certified traps territory-wide: the GNWT Summary states 'It is unlawful for any person to use traps not listed in the regulations. Only approved certified traps listed in the Agreement on International Humane Trapping Standards may be used in the NWT.' The Genuine Mackenzie Valley Fur program also complies with the AIHTS. Unlike Ontario, the requirement is not species-scheduled in published territorial material — it reads as a blanket certified-traps rule for trapping. AIHTS was agreed in 1997 and ratified by Canada in June 1999; the FIC maintains the national certified list.
trap_rules: Only AIHTS-certified traps may be used in the NWT; it is unlawful to use traps not listed in the regulations (GNWT Summary, Wildlife Regulation notice).
Live-hold restraining traps (soft-catch traps / leg snares) must be checked at least once every 72 hours (ECC).
Trapping equipment must not be set before the first day of a season and must be removed or rendered harmless by the last day of the season (GNWT Summary).

Pelt wastage is an offence for bear*, beaver*, coyote, ermine, fisher, fox, least weasel, lynx, marten, mink, muskrat*, otter, skunk, wolf and wolverine (*pelts may be discarded where the animal was harvested for meat).

aihts.canada_wide: AIHTS in force in Canada since 1 June 1999 (Canada, the EU and Russia are parties; the US is not a party). FIC-certified traps mandatory per Phase 1 lists - killing traps: beaver, Canada lynx & bobcat, fisher, marten, muskrat (on land and underwater), otter, raccoon, weasels/ermine; restraining traps: beaver (cage), bobcat, Canada lynx, raccoon, wolf. Conventional steel-jawed leghold restraining traps on land are effectively banned for AIHTS species. Killing neck snares are NOT AIHTS traps and are not FIC-certified; provinces regulate snares separately. [R1 s.2a]

check_interval.live_holding: Restraining traps (live-hold soft catch or leg snare): at least once every 72 hours (GNWT official trapping page; GNWT Summary of Hunting and Trapping Regulations).
check_interval.killing: No interval stated for killing traps or killing snares.
check_interval.note: Confidence: official guide / government page - the underlying Trapping Regulations text was not located online (R2 Item 1). Supersedes R1, which found no NWT interval.

canada_only.tenure: Registered trapping areas / registered group trapping areas in some areas; otherwise rights-based harvesting plus Special Trapping Licences for non-rights holders (typically only at an Aboriginal community's request).
canada_only.trap_id_requirement: None found - no trap owner-ID marking requirement in the sources searched (follow-up pass, Nov 17); identification runs through licence/tenure and pelt seals instead.
canada_only.royalty: None found - the Wildlife Fees Regulations R-114-2014 list fees only and the Wildlife Act has no royalty provision; the GNWT instead pays trappers through the Genuine Mackenzie Valley Fur Program. [R2 Item 5]
canada_only.nuisance_route: None found - Wildlife Act ss. 55-56 self-help (chase wildlife away; kill if necessary to prevent injury/death or property damage); problem-wildlife response is officer-led (Renewable Resource Officers). No NWCO licence or paid-trapper program found. [R2 Item 3]
